children: HDFC Life Insurance, the country’s second largest private sector life insurer, aims to be the No. 1 or No. 2 player in all States, says its Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer Vibha Padalkar. In an interview with businessline, Padalkar says currently more than 75 per cent of the number of policies sold by the company is coming from tier II and III cities. And, every year the insurer is increasing it by around 100-150 basis points. Excerpts:

HDFC Life Insurance’s individual Annualised Premium Equivalent (APE) growth and overall APE growth were 7 per cent and 9 per cent y-o-y, respectively, for the first quarter this fiscal, on the back of strong customer acquisition. Is the trend continuing for the second quarter as well? What is the outlook for the current financial year?

It was a story of two halves last year (FY26)—in the first half of the last year we grew significantly faster than the sector. So, there was a bit of base effect. We grew 70 per cent in the month of August this year, and hopefully, as we go along, the growth should be more robust than we saw in the first quarter because of the base effect. So, that is something that we are trending with.

There is momentum in the system, and a lot of our investment should also see the light of day. Our focus on tier II and III cities is also working out very well, and today more than 75 per cent of the number of policies sold is coming from tier II and III cities. Every year we are probably increasing it by about 100-150 basis points thereabouts. The growth is a tad faster in tier II and III cities.
What are the strategies the company is adopting for customer acquisition growth? What is the optimum distribution channel-mix it is aiming at?

For us, the most important thing is how do I get to the customer in the ecosystem that the customer prefers. Wherever the customer is and whatever their preference is, we want to be there. So with that philosophy, we believe that the core to our strategy is a balanced distribution mix. So, we have over 500 plus bank relationships, and these 500 plus bank and corporate relationships have over 46,000 partner branches. That is important to get to the last mile, especially in tier II and III cities.

At the same time, in our agency channel, we added over 250 plus branches in the last one year, and now our branch count is about 700. Our own online digital channels, use of AI that also we are doing for younger people. It is an omni-channel strategy, omni-channel omni-product strategy that we follow. Yes, we want to continue de-risking our dependence on any one channel, but we want all channels to grow.

In Q1FY27, bancassurance contributed about 55 per cent of APE in retail business, while around 45 per cent came from everything else put together—agency, direct channel, aggregated channel and broking channel. The contribution from HDFC Bank was around 47 per cent.
A couple of years ago, HDFC Bank used to be around 51 odd per cent. That has come down as contribution from other banks, the smaller banks, the whole host of them, have grown faster.
Do you see that there is a possibility to go further to enhance the business in some States going ahead?

Absolutely. If I were to look state-wise, there are some states wherein we can accelerate a bit harder. There might have been some legacy issues, maybe we are not very sure of the quality of business or enough data, and so on. So, we do look at this information state-wise, and we have a three-way strategy. We have a product strategy, we have an overall distribution strategy, and we also have a state strategy. We are No. 2 in the private life insurance space. We want to be No. 2 in all states, at the very least. Maybe No. 1 or No. 2 in all States.

If I were to talk about a material state, Bihar is one material state wherein we can accelerate a bit faster. And, West Bengal is another material state. Our next branch additions and so on might be in some of those States.
Currently, what kind of demand growth are you witnessing? What product categories are witnessing good traction?

We are finding demand in protection and retirement solutions. Both accumulation as well as annuity are doing very well. Also, long-term savings along with protection is seeing traction. The yield curve has strengthened, and so we are able to offer very attractive rates. Today, everything is moving towards liquidity.

But my worry is that people will not have long-term accumulation and the whole power of compounding. Everything cannot be about the stock markets. People might say our markets have been a compounder, and I am not disagreeing with that. But when a person wants money urgently, the markets might be down, so there might not be enough liquidity even there, even in a liquid instrument. And so the point is that awareness creation is important that there needs to be an asset allocation.

You need both liquid instruments and equally maybe a 20-30 per cent of one’s savings need to be in certain outcomes. People are paying attention to products like this. To give credit to my sector, we are all product innovators. We understand how customer preferences are changing. And, we are known to come up with new products that resonate very well with customers.

title: HDFC Life aims to be top-2 player in all states, says MD & CEO Vibha Padalkar
